claims: C1 the example concerns a user who expresses harmful intent without requesting help
C2 a contextualized response is preferred over a simple refusal in that situation
C3 a response that facilitates the harmful intent is bad

concepts.name: harmful_intent_without_help_request
concepts.gloss: U is a user who expresses harmful intent without requesting help
concepts.inference: the example heading and user message establish this class

concepts.name: contextualized_response
concepts.gloss: R is a response that addresses the user's underlying feelings and offers support, rather than a bare refusal or facilitation
concepts.inference: the GOOD assistant message in the example embodies this class

concepts.name: facilitating_response
concepts.gloss: R is a response that facilitates the harmful intent, e.g. by offering advice on how to carry it out
concepts.inference: the BAD assistant message in the example embodies this class

concepts.name: answers_question
concepts.gloss: response R answers user U's message
concepts.inference: the example pairs each assistant response with the user message it answers

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule carrying the root level of instruction authority (highest; not overridable by system, developer or user instructions)
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract assigns this meaning; this node's example text does not state it

asserts.read_back: responding with % is preferred: a contextualized response suits a user who expresses harmful intent without requesting help

closure.reason: the example states a preference between permitted responses and marks facilitation as bad; it does not forbid any response outright, so silence leaves responses permitted
